title: What is known about 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_0RA1LC_1RA1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_0RA1LC_1RA1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is always two blocks side by side, an alternating block (10)^x and a solid block 1^y, and the machine shuttles cells from one to the other by doubling. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; an exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells, runs crossed at once) finds no halt in the first 1015 steps. Lean proves both phase rules of the doubling (below) for all sizes.

What Lean proves. The whole phase map, every case for all sizes (E(x, z) = E>0 (10)^x 1^z, A(x, y) = (10)^x 1^y A>0 and the bounce frame Q(m, j, t) = (10)^m 1 D>0 0 (1010)^j 1^t), and halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the map, iterated from A(0, 0) (the blank tape), reaches E(x, 0) or E(x, 1). By native_decide the first 108 phases (about 4.1·1021 machine steps) do not. Lean also proves that the even phases lead only to even phases or to an all-ones tape, and checks, for every all-ones tape of length n < 105, that its run halts before the next even phase or all-ones tape exactly when n is 1 or 12·2k − 2k − 9 (3, 13, 35, 81, 175, …). lean/Fatal.lean proves that list for every n, by the kernel (ones_fatal_all, ones_safe_all). What is not proved: that the run never lands on a fatal length.

Where a halt would come from. The halting transition F0 fires only when state E stands on the 0 at the left end with at most one 1 after the alternating block. Probing every two-block tape with x, y < 150 shows that a parity rule keeps that from happening, except right after the tape has become all ones, 1^n: from 1^n A>0 the machine halts exactly for n = 1, 3, 6, 13, 35, 81, 175, 365, … (n = 12·2k − 2k − 9 and two small values, checked up to n = 400).

Why it has not halted. All-ones moments are rare: eleven in the first 109 steps, at n = 5, 10, 14, 30, 61, 89, 169, 222, 382, 542 and 781, none of them in the halting list, and only five more by step 1015 (n = 9705, 59501, 77694, 271974, 311881). A halt needs an all-ones moment to land exactly on a number of that sparse list, so the machine very probably never halts, but nothing here proves it.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 4,184 cells have been visited and 3,482 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.336). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.336).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact macro simulator (c/mrun.c: the tape cut into blocks of 2 cells, run-length coded, a run crossed at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with) runs 1015 steps without a halt. It agrees with the plain simulator tools/c/tmrun at 109 steps.

claims.title: The two phase rules, along the run
claims.text: Write E(x,z) for the tape E>0 (10)^x 1^z (blank around) and A(x,y) for (10)^x 1^y A>0. Of the 2,085 such moments in the first 109 steps, every left phase with z ≥ 2x + 8 went E(x,z) → E(2x+4, z−2x−6) (507 times) and every right phase with y even and 2x ≥ y + 2 went A(x,y) → A(x−y/2, 2y+2) (534 times).

claims.title: The two phase rules, for all sizes
claims.text: Lean proves, with rfl steps, the crossing lemmas and induction on the number of bounces: E(x,z) reaches E(2x+4, z−2x−6) whenever x ≥ 1 and z ≥ 2x + 7 (ephase), and A(x,y) reaches A(x−y/2, 2y+2) whenever y ≥ 4 is even and 2x ≥ y + 2 (aphase). Both phases are made of the same bounce, (10)^(m+1) 1 D>0 0 (1010)^j 1^(r+3) to (10)^m 1 D>0 0 (1010)^(j+1) 1^(r+1) in 8j + 10 steps, plus a start and an end piece generated by py/gen_rules.py. The parity analysis is proved separately, on the whole phase map (even_next in lean/Phases.lean).

claims.title: Step counts of the phases
claims.text: Probing from those tapes, E(x,z) → E(2x+4, z−2x−6) takes 4x² + 24x + 30 steps and A(x,y) → A(x−y/2, 2y+2) takes y² + 2y + 6 steps (checked for small x, y; the step counts of the Lean pieces add up to the same formulas). Doubling costs the square of the block, so a tape of width w takes about w³ steps to grow: the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>.

claims.title: Halting needs an all-ones tape from a sparse list
claims.text: From every two-block tape E(x,z) and A(x,y) with x, z, y < 150 the next two-block tape was computed. Call E(x,z) with z even and z ≥ 2, and A(x,y) with x ≥ 1 and y even, even: every even tape leads to an even tape or to an all-ones tape 1^n A>0, never to a halt. The machine halts only from E(x,0) or E(x,1). From 1^n A>0 it halts exactly when n is 1, 3, 6, 13, 35, 81, 175 or 365 (n ≤ 400), the list n = 12·2k − 2k − 9 plus 1 and 6. Not proved for all sizes.

claims.title: All-ones moments so far
claims.text: In the first 109 steps the tape is 1^n A>0 eleven times: n = 5, 10, 14, 30, 61, 89, 169, 222, 382, 542, 781 (the last at step 6,712,466). None is in the halting list. Between 109 and 1015 steps, five more (from the exact macro simulation, which recognises the moment 1^(n+1) <C that follows 1^n A>0): n = 9705, 59501, 77694, 271974, 311881, at steps 1.26·1010, 2.92·1012, 6.51·1012, 2.80·1014 and 4.21·1014. None is in the list; the nearest members are 12259, 49119, 98269, 196571 and 393177.

claims.title: The whole phase map
claims.text: Write E(x, z) = E>0 (10)^x 1^z, A(x, y) = (10)^x 1^y A>0 and the bounce frame Q(m, j, t) = (10)^m 1 D>0 0 (1010)^j 1^t. next sends each of them to the next one the machine reaches (bounces taken all at once), with 21 cases; next_sound proves every case for all parameters (one symbolic run of lean/Pieces.lean each, generated by py/pieces.py, and induction for the bounces). next fails only at E(x, 0) and E(x, 1), which halt (e_halts).

claims.title: Halts if and only if the map reaches E(x, 0) or E(x, 1)
claims.text: halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some iterate of next from A(0, 0) (the blank tape) is E(x, z) with z ≤ 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> phases
claims.text: no_halt_phases, by native_decide: the first 108 iterates are defined and none is E(x, 0) or E(x, 1). By the step counts of the pieces (py/phasemap.py run) that is about 4.1·1021 machine steps.

claims.title: The parity classes
claims.text: even_next: the even phases (E(x, z) with z even and z ≥ 2, A(x, y) with x ≥ 1 and y even, Q(m, j, t) with t even) lead only to even phases or to an all-ones tape. So from an even phase the machine cannot halt before the tape is next all ones (even_safe).

claims.title: The fatal all-ones lengths below 10<sup>5</sup>
claims.text: fatal_list, by native_decide: for every n < 105, the run from the all-ones tape A(0, n) reaches a halting phase before an even phase or another all-ones tape exactly when n is 1 or 12·2k − 2k − 9 (3, 13, 35, 81, 175, …) (ones_fatal, ones_safe). For every n it is proved by the kernel in lean/Fatal.lean.

claims.title: The fatal all-ones lengths, for every n
claims.text: ones_fatal_all: for every n with n = 1 or n = 12·2k − 2k − 9 for some k, the machine halts from the all-ones tape A(0, n). ones_safe_all: for every other n, any iterate of next from A(0, n) that halts comes after another all-ones tape. The proof: from E(x, z) with z odd the run is a chain of doublings E(x, z) → E(2x+4, z−2x−6) that halts exactly when z = zHalt(x, k) (e_fate, strong induction on z), with zHalt(x, k) closed-form (zHalt_closed).

claims.title: All-ones moments in the first 10<sup>8</sup> phases
claims.text: Iterating the map with the pieces' step counts (py/phasemap.py run 100000000): after n = 311881 (step 4.21·1014) the tape is all ones at n = 523702, 1318973, 2121389, 3762174, 10123517, 17586302 and 44891446 (the last near step 1.26·1021). None is fatal.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It would need an all-ones tape whose length is in a sparse list; nothing rules that out.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, but the reason is now clear. The tape is an alternating block next to a solid block; the machine doubles one at the other's expense, back and forth. It can only halt right after the tape becomes all ones, and only if the number of ones is in a sparse list (3, 13, 35, 81, 175, …).

facts.text: No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> phases of the phase map proved in Lean (about 4.1·10<sup>21</sup> machine steps).
It halts if and only if the phase map, iterated from the start, reaches E(x, 0) or E(x, 1).
The all-ones tape of length n halts before the next all-ones tape exactly when n is 1 or 12·2<sup>k</sup> − 2k − 9 (3, 13, 35, 81, 175, …), proved for all n.
No halt in an exact macro simulation (blocks of 2 cells, runs crossed at once).
The tape is always an alternating block and a solid block; each phase doubles one of them.
From an all-ones tape it halts exactly for n = 3, 13, 35, 81, 175, … (checked to n = 400).
E(x,z) → E(2x+4, z−2x−6) and A(x,y) → A(x−y/2, 2y+2), proved in Lean for all sizes.
No halt in the C simulator; 4,184 cells visited.

sections.heading: Two blocks
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell and the tape always looks the same: an alternating block 10 10 10 … followed by a solid block of 1s. Writing a for 10, here are four moments around step 7·107:

The alternating block grows from 8 copies to 18, 40, 84, 172, 348, 700: it roughly doubles each time, eating the solid block. When the solid block is too short for another doubling the machine turns to the right end and the roles swap: now the solid block doubles (a^541 1^642, a^220 1^1286) and eats the alternating one.

sections.heading: Doubling, back and forth
html: Write E(x,z) for the tape E>0 (10)^x 1^z, the head in state E at the left end, and A(x,y) for (10)^x 1^y A>0, the head in state A just past the right end.

• Left phase. E(x,z) → E(2x+4, z−2x−6), as long as z ≥ 2x+8. The head bounces between the alternating block and the solid block; each bounce moves one 10 from the left part to the right part and turns two solid 1s into another 10. It takes 4x²+24x+30 steps.
  • Right phase. A(x,y) → A(x−y/2, 2y+2) for even y, as long as x is large enough: the solid block doubles, eating the alternating block. It takes y²+2y+6 steps.

When a doubling no longer fits, the machine switches phase, and the width of the tape grows by a couple of cells. Both rules held at every one of the 1,041 doublings in the first 109 steps. Since a doubling of a block of size x costs about x² steps and the tape grows by a few cells per phase change, a tape of width w takes about w³ steps: that is why the width grows like the cube root of the step count.

In effect the machine runs the doubling map: the split point between the two blocks moves like x ↦ 2x around a circle of the tape's width, the classic example of a chaotic map. The exact remainders at each overflow decide everything.

sections.heading: Halting needs a perfect landing
html: The halting transition is F reading a 0. State F is entered only from E reading a 0 (1RF), and E and F together walk right over 0 1 0 1 …. So the machine halts only when E starts at the left end with at most one 1 after the alternating block: E>0 (10)^x or E>0 (10)^x 1. A left phase reaches that when z − 2x − 6 = 1: the doubling has to use up the solid block exactly, leaving a single 1.

Parity forbids it in the normal course of things. Probing every two-block tape with x, y, z < 150: if z is even at the left phase and y is even at the right phase, the next two-block tape is again of that kind, or the tape becomes all ones. Only an all-ones tape 1^n can start a left phase with z odd, and from 1^n A>0 the run halts exactly when
n = 1, 3, 6, 13, 35, 81, 175, 365, …   (n = 12·2k − 2k − 9 for k ≥ 0, and 1, 6),

checked directly for every n ≤ 400. The reason: from 1^n the alternating block restarts at x = 2 and goes 2, 8, 20, 44, 92, … (x ↦ 2x+4), each doubling taking 2x+6 ones; the run halts if the ones run out leaving exactly one.

sections.heading: Rare resets, sparse targets
html: The tape becomes all ones only when a right phase lands exactly on x = 0. That happened eleven times in the first 109 steps, at n = 5, 10, 14, 30, 61, 89, 169, 222, 382, 542, 781, and the last of them was at step 6.7·106. Between 109 and 1015 steps there were only five more: n = 9705, 59501, 77694, 271974, 311881. None was in the halting list.

A crude model: a phase change lands on an exact value with chance about 1/w on a tape of width w, so all-ones moments become rarer as the tape grows, and each one also has to hit a list whose members double. Under that model the expected number of halts from here on is small and shrinking: the machine very probably never halts. Turning that into a proof would mean controlling the exact remainders of a doubling map, which is as hard as questions about the binary digits of specific numbers.

Two near-duplicates, 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_1LA1LC_1RA1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE and 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_1RA1LC_0RB1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE, share the left phase (states D, E, F and B) and behave the same way, each with its own sparse list of fatal all-ones lengths.

sections.heading: The phase map in Lean
html: Every configuration the run passes through at a phase boundary is one of three shapes: E(x, z) = E>0 (10)^x 1^z, A(x, y) = (10)^x 1^y A>0 and the bounce frame Q(m, j, t) = (10)^m 1 D>0 0 (1010)^j 1^t. The function next in lean/Phases.lean sends each one to the next shape the machine reaches, and next_sound proves each of its 21 cases for all parameters, from symbolic runs generated by py/pieces.py. Nothing is left out: next is undefined only at E(x, 0) and E(x, 1), and those halt.

So the question is exactly whether the orbit of A(0, 0) (the blank tape) under next reaches E(x, 0) or E(x, 1) (halts_iff). The first 108 iterates do not (native_decide); by the step counts that is about 4.1·1021 machine steps. The even phases cannot reach a halt without an all-ones tape in between, and for all-ones tapes shorter than 105 cells Lean checks which ones lead to a halt first: n = 1 or 12·2k − 2k − 9 (3, 13, 35, 81, 175, …). lean/Fatal.lean proves that list for every n: from E(x, z) with z odd the run is a chain of doublings E(x, z) → E(2x+4, z−2x−6), which halts exactly when z = zHalt(x, k) for some k (e_fate, strong induction on z), and zHalt(2, k) = 12·2k − 2k − 11 (zHalt_closed). The last open step is to show that the run never hits a fatal length.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.336). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.336).
After 109 steps the tape spans 4,184 cells (1,677 left of the start, 1,716 right), with a density of 1s of 0.832.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: doubling between an alternating and a solid block
summary: Two blocks, (10)^x and 1^y, take turns doubling at each other's expense; it halts only if an all-ones tape 1^n ever has n = 12·2^k − 2k − 9, and that has not happened.
